title: Clipping and cutting the cystic duct

limitations: Stage order, tool choice, clip positions and feedback are a draft written by the software team from the VID01 annotations. A qualified surgeon or educator has not reviewed them.
The anatomy is a generic BodyParts3D model, not the patient in the video. The cystic artery is a schematic drawing.
Placement and gestures are discrete software interactions. They do not model force, tissue response or real instrument handling.

objective: Expose the cystic duct, close it with two clips and divide it between them, in order, on a schematic model.

action_points.label: Cystic duct, common bile duct side

stages.title: Expose the duct
stages.instruction: Hold the gallbladder by its neck and lift it, so the cystic duct is on view.

feedback.tool: This instrument does not hold tissue. Look for one with blunt, ridged jaws.
feedback.target: That structure is not the gallbladder. Find the gallbladder itself.
feedback.placement: That is the gallbladder, but this spot does not lift the neck toward you. Hold it closer to where it narrows into the duct.
feedback.success: The neck is held and lifted, which opens the space around the cystic duct.

stages.rationale: Lifting the gallbladder neck stretches the cystic duct so it can be seen clearly before anything is closed.
stages.reference_note: VID01 annotation: grasper retracts the gallbladder, 670 to 675 s.

stages.title: First clip
stages.instruction: Close the cystic duct with a clip on the side toward the common bile duct, leaving room for a second clip.

feedback.tool: This instrument cannot close a duct. Look for the one that carries a small metal clip in its jaws.
feedback.target: That structure is not the cystic duct. This stage closes the cystic duct only.
feedback.placement: That is the cystic duct, but this clip goes on the side toward the common bile duct, with room left for another clip.
feedback.success: The first clip closes the cystic duct on the common bile duct side.

stages.rationale: A clip on the side that stays in the body keeps bile from leaking once the duct is divided.
stages.reference_note: VID01 annotation: clip applier clips the cystic duct, 698 to 747 s.

stages.title: Second clip
stages.instruction: Place a second clip on the cystic duct, this time on the gallbladder side.

feedback.tool: This instrument cannot close a duct. You need the same kind of instrument as the last stage.
feedback.target: That structure is not the cystic duct. This stage closes the cystic duct only.
feedback.placement: That is the cystic duct, but this clip goes on the gallbladder side, leaving a gap after the first clip.
feedback.success: The duct is now closed on both sides, with a gap between the clips.

stages.rationale: A clip on the gallbladder side stops its contents spilling when the duct is divided, and leaves a gap to cut in.
stages.reference_note: VID01 annotation: clip applier clips the cystic duct, 815 to 844 s.

stages.title: Divide the duct
stages.instruction: Divide the cystic duct in the gap between the two clips.

feedback.tool: This instrument does not divide a clipped duct. Look for one with two fine blades.
feedback.target: That structure is not the cystic duct. Only the clipped duct is divided in this stage.
feedback.placement: That is the cystic duct, but the cut goes in the gap between the two clips, not through or beside one.
feedback.success: The duct is divided between the clips, so each end stays closed.

stages.rationale: Cutting between the clips leaves a closed end on both the body side and the gallbladder side.
stages.reference_note: VID01 annotation: scissors cut the cystic duct, 860 to 877 s.
